title: Loop language: unsat cores
description: Graphs on n nodes that can be 3-coloured. Here a candidate is good when the check is satisfiable; a bad candidate is refined with the core of the failed check. Compare with the Reference run in the comment at the end of the loop script.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any graph.
{ edge(X,Y) : node(X), node(Y), X < Y }.
#show edge/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A witness, not a counterexample: a proper 3-colouring of the candidate.
% If there is none, the candidate is wrong, and the unsat core says which
% edges are to blame.
1 { col(N,1..3) } 1 :- node(N).
:- edge(X,Y), col(X,C), col(Y,C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Here the check looks for a witness. A candidate without one is rejected;
# G.core(C) is the refinement built from the unsatisfiable core of the last
# C.solve: the edges that together make 3-colouring impossible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        if not C.solve(assume G(M)):
            reject M with G.core(C)

# For comparison, the reference run blocks each bad candidate:
#         if not C.solve(assume G(M)):
#             reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Here the check looks for a witness. A candidate without one is rejected;
# G.core(C) is the refinement built from the unsatisfiable core of the last
# C.solve: the edges that together make 3-colouring impossible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        if not C.solve(assume G(M)):
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Here the check looks for a witness. A candidate without one is rejected;
# G.core(C) is the refinement built from the unsatisfiable core of the last
# C.solve: the edges that together make 3-colouring impossible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        if not C.solve(assume G(M)):
            reject M with C.core.minimal.on(G)
